key_strengths: Top-tier publication record in African art history — Art Bulletin, African Arts, NKa, Yale UP, Tate, Bloomsbury
Deep single-site expertise in Ekiti/Yoruba masquerade over three decades — unusual depth and longitudinal access
Proven track record with AHRC, British Academy, Henry Moore Foundation, Arts Council England, and EU FP7
High-profile live museum project (John Randle Museum, Lagos) demonstrating public engagement and international institutional reach
Strong PhD supervision pipeline across African, Caribbean, and European art topics (4 current students)
Extensive network of museum, institutional, and policy roles — British Library, Vatican, UCL, Ford Foundation, Oxford Dictionary of African Art
Two manuscripts at advanced stages (one in peer review at James Currey, one commissioned by Cambridge UP) — strong pipeline for next funding cycle
potential_gaps: No PI grant of significant scale held independently in over 15 years (last major PI grant was Henry Moore Foundation 2006–2009)
Published monograph output is thin — only one book (1997, 64pp); major monographs remain in preparation
No ERC, Horizon Europe, or Horizon UK experience listed
Career level is Senior Lecturer, not Professor — some fellowship schemes (e.g. Leverhulme Major Research Fellowship) favour professorial applicants
AHRC WROCAH involvement was as bid team member, not PI or CoI — limited direct AHRC project management track record
Limited visible international collaborative network outside UK–Nigeria axis
